subject: wright-brothers
title: Two Brothers Learn to Fly
summary: How the Wright brothers practiced, tested, and finally flew.

cards.title: Count to 12
cards.text: Count to 12 out loud, slowly. That is how long the very first airplane flight lasted. It happened on December 17, 1903.

cards.title: Bike shop builders
cards.text: Wilbur and Orville Wright lived in Dayton, Ohio, and ran a bicycle shop. In 1896 they started to study flying for real. They read all they could find, and Wilbur even wrote to the Smithsonian to ask for more.

cards.title: Practice first
cards.text: Before they added an engine, the brothers built gliders. In 1902 alone, they made between 700 and 1,000 glides. They learned to steer by twisting the tips of the wings.
cards.example: Wilbur said, "It is possible to fly without motors, but not without knowledge and skill."

cards.title: Test, fail, fix
cards.text: Their early gliders did not lift as much as the math said they should. So in 1901 they built a small wind tunnel. They tested lots of tiny wing shapes and wrote down what really happened.
cards.example: Their next glider, built with the new numbers, worked much better.

cards.title: The big day
cards.text: At Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville flew for 12 seconds and went 120 feet. Later that day, Wilbur flew 852 feet in 59 seconds. Then a gust of wind flipped the plane. It never flew again, but you can see it in a museum in Washington, D.C.

cards.question: The Wright brothers failed many times before they flew. Why do you think they kept going?
nudges: What did each mistake teach them?
Think of something you got better at by messing up first.

questions.q: What did the Wright brothers do before they added an engine?

options.why: Yes! Hundreds of glides taught them how to control a plane.

options.text: They bought a plane from a store.
options.why: There were no airplanes to buy yet. They had to invent one.
Balloons were different. The brothers practiced with gliders.

questions.q: Why did they build a wind tunnel?

options.text: Their gliders did not lift as much as the math said, so they tested wing shapes.
options.why: Right. They checked the numbers for themselves.

options.text: To make wind at Kitty Hawk
options.why: Kitty Hawk already had strong, steady winds. That is why they went there.
The tunnel was for testing small wings, not the engine.

questions.q: How long was the very first flight?

options.why: Correct. Short, but it was a real powered flight with a pilot.
Much shorter than that. It was 12 seconds.
Long flights came later. In 1905 Wilbur flew for 39 minutes.
